publications.title: Constitution of the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets (TCCFM)
publications.summary: In pursuance of the announcement made in the Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies dated October 7, 2026 , the Reserve Bank of India announces the constitution of the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets (TCCFM) against the backdrop of rapidly evolving financial markets and infrastructure. The Committee will serve as a forum for structured engagement with market participants and stakeholders by the Reserve Bank on policy and operational matters related to money, government securities and foreign exchange markets as well as the respective derivative markets and infrastructure. 2. The Committee will be Chaired by the Deputy Governor (DG) in charge of the Financial Markets Regulation Department (FMRD) of the Reserve Bank of India. publications.title: Act now to be resilient in the quantum future
publications.summary: Quantum computing will bring significant opportunities to the UK financial sector, but firms need to act now to prepare for a world where a viable hostile quantum computer could break today’s widely used cryptography standards.The financial sector depends on secure information and communication. Cryptography – of which encryption is just one part – helps firms protect their clients’ data, verify who they are dealing with, and maintain trust in their systems.Sufficiently powerful quantum computers pose a real threat to that security. Without trustworthy cryptography, consumers would face fraud, firms would suffer operational disruption, and the integrity of financial transactions and markets would be put at risk.That’s why we are talking to firms about preparing for post-quantum cryptography (PQC) now.
